results.result: Costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency reduce IL-2 production in T cells. IL-2 amounts in supernatants and IL-2 mRNA levels were significantly reduced upon blockade of CD80/CD86 and in Itk-deficient T cells, particularly at lower peptide concentrations. IL-2 mRNA generation occurred during the first six hours of T cell activation, consistent with transient NFκB nuclear localization and prior findings that brief APC contact commits T cells to proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 provide converging evidence from IL-2 protein measurements (C1), IL-2 mRNA quantification with statistical significance (C2), time course data (C3), and citation to prior work (C4). The data consistently demonstrate that attenuation of T cell activation reduces IL-2 production, with appropriate statistical support (p<0.001) and temporal characterization.

results.result: Costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency reduce central accumulation of signaling proteins at the T cell:APC interface, which correlates with reduced cSMAC formation and efficient IL-2 secretion. Sensors that displayed frequent central accumulation under full stimulus showed diminished central localization upon costimulation blockade and in Itk-deficient T cells, particularly during the first two minutes of cell coupling.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C8 establish a correlation between reduced central protein accumulation and reduced IL-2 production under attenuated activation conditions. The imaging data (C5, C6) support the interpretation of reduced cSMAC formation (C7), and the association with IL-2 secretion (C8) is consistently observed across multiple conditions. However, the causal relationship is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

results.result: LAT displays biphasic central accumulation at the T cell:APC interface that is significantly reduced by costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency. Under full stimulus, 49±6% of cell couples showed central LAT accumulation at tight coupling, dropping to ~25% after 2 minutes. Costimulation blockade reduced the initial peak to 11±4% (p<0.001), and Itk deficiency reduced it to 26±6% (p=0.005), with the combination yielding the least accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C14 provide detailed quantitative characterization of LAT localization dynamics with appropriate statistical analysis. The biphasic pattern is clearly documented (C9-C11), and the effects of costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency are quantified with statistical significance (C12-C14). The data are internally consistent and support the temporal and condition-dependent regulation of LAT accumulation.

results.result: Impaired cytoskeletal transport processes contribute to diminished central LAT accumulation upon costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency. Enhancement of actin dynamics with constitutively active Rac and Cofilin significantly increased (p<0.001) central and overall LAT accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C16 provide experimental evidence linking actin dynamics to LAT accumulation. The rescue experiment with active Rac and Cofilin (C16) supports the inference that impaired cytoskeletal transport contributes to reduced LAT accumulation (C15). The statistical significance (p<0.001) and citation to prior work strengthen the conclusion, though the mechanism remains partially inferred.

results.result: LAT phosphorylation at Y191 is diminished upon costimulation blockade and Itk deficiency. At 2, 5, and 10 minutes after tight cell coupling, LAT phosphorylation was significantly reduced (p≤0.02) in Itk-deficient T cells upon costimulation blockade by 39%, 61%, and 70%, respectively, compared to wild type under full stimulus.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C18 provide Western blot data with quantification and statistical analysis demonstrating reduced LAT phosphorylation under attenuated activation conditions. The temporal progression and quantitative measurements with statistical significance support the conclusion. The data are consistent with the reduced LAT accumulation observed in imaging experiments.

results.result: The cSMAC contains multiple supramolecular LAT/pLAT complexes of 0.23-0.25 μm³ volume. STED super-resolution microscopy revealed an average of four LAT/pLAT complexes per cell, with complexes in the cSMAC region being significantly larger (p=0.04 for LAT, p=0.007 for pLAT) than those in non-cSMAC regions (0.12-0.13 μm³).
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C21 provide quantitative super-resolution microscopy data characterizing the size and number of LAT/pLAT complexes in the cSMAC. The statistical significance of size differences between cSMAC and non-cSMAC regions is documented. The use of STED microscopy is appropriate for resolving supramolecular structures, and the quantification appears rigorous.

results.result: The cSMAC is associated with extensive membrane undulations. The ratio of plasma membrane length to straight-line diameter was significantly larger (p<0.001) in the cSMAC (2.2±0.3) than in the pSMAC (1.4±0.1). Control cell couples without cSMAC formation showed a ratio of 1.5±0.1, similar to pSMAC regions, indicating that membrane undulations are specifically enhanced in the cSMAC.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C24 provide electron microscopy measurements with statistical analysis demonstrating enhanced membrane undulations in the cSMAC. The comparison between cSMAC, pSMAC, and control conditions is appropriate, and the statistical significance is clearly documented. The inference that the cSMAC is a region of enhanced protein proximity (C24) is reasonable based on the structural data.

results.result: Protein domains used for LAT targeting have distinct localization properties. The PKCθ V3 domain is required for PKCθ central accumulation but cannot drive central localization alone. The Vav1 SH3SH2SH3 domains drive strong central accumulation only within the first minute of cell coupling. The PLCδ PH domain mediates interface accumulation during the first two minutes without central preference.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C28 characterize the localization properties of protein domains used for LAT targeting. The data combine citations to prior work (C25) with imaging data showing temporal and spatial localization patterns (C26-C28). The characterization is important for interpreting the LAT fusion protein experiments that follow.

results.result: GFP fusion proteins were expressed at 2.1±0.7 fold the endogenous level of LAT in non-transduced T cells, with little change to endogenous LAT levels in transduced cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C29 provides Western blot quantification data documenting expression levels of fusion proteins. This is an important control demonstrating that fusion proteins are expressed at near-physiological levels, which is critical for interpreting functional effects. The data appear straightforward and well-controlled.

results.result: LAT V3 fusion stabilizes central LAT accumulation beyond physiological levels. LAT V3 yielded efficient central accumulation sustained over the entire imaging time frame at ~50% of cell couples under all conditions. Starting 40s after tight cell coupling, this was significantly more frequent (p<0.05) than non-targeted LAT under full stimulus. Membrane undulations in LAT V3-expressing cells were similar to LAT-expressing cells, supporting comparable cSMAC properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C33 characterize the LAT V3 fusion protein with imaging and electron microscopy data. The sustained central accumulation is well-documented with statistical analysis (C31), and the comparison to physiological LAT localization (C32) is appropriate. The electron microscopy data (C33) provide important validation that LAT V3 forms structurally similar cSMACs despite altered dynamics.

results.result: LAT Vav fusion has condition-dependent effects on LAT localization. Under full stimulus, LAT Vav showed diminished central and overall accumulation compared to LAT alone (p<0.05), suggesting it does not enhance properly assembled signaling complexes. However, upon attenuated stimuli, LAT Vav consistently enhanced central accumulation (p≤0.001 for costimulation blockade), with accumulation patterns largely indistinguishable from non-targeted LAT under full stimulus (p>0.05), allowing fairly close reconstitution of full stimulus-type LAT localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C38 document the complex, condition-dependent behavior of LAT Vav with appropriate statistical analysis. The negative effect under full stimulus (C34-C35) and rescue under attenuated conditions (C36-C37) are both well-supported by imaging data. The interpretation that LAT Vav reconstitutes physiological LAT localization under attenuated conditions (C38) is reasonable based on the quantitative comparisons.

results.result: LAT PLCδPH fusion partially restores LAT accumulation under attenuated conditions. LAT PLCδPH resembled LAT Vav but was less powerful. Upon attenuated stimuli, LAT PLCδPH moderately enhanced central and overall LAT accumulation but didn't consistently reach the same extent as LAT alone under full stimulus. For example, in Itk-deficient T cells upon costimulation blockade, interface accumulation increased from <32% to >55% (p<0.005).
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C41 characterize LAT PLCδPH as an intermediate between LAT Vav and non-targeted LAT in terms of rescue efficacy. The imaging data with statistical analysis support this characterization. The specific example (C41) provides quantitative evidence for partial rescue, though the overall effect is less consistent than LAT Vav.

results.result: LAT fusion constructs show substantial interface recruitment and are functional. All LAT constructs showed substantial interface recruitment with moderately less LAT Vav recruitment at late time points. The targeted LAT constructs were tyrosine phosphorylated upon T cell activation. Fusion of LAT with additional protein interaction domains allowed control of central clustering, with PKCθ V3 yielding enhanced central localization, Vav1 SH3SH2SH3 largely restoring full stimulus-type localization upon attenuation, and PLCδ PH resulting in partial restoration.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C44 provide important controls and summary of LAT fusion protein properties. The computational quantification of interface enrichment (C42) and Western blot data showing phosphorylation (C43) validate that the fusion proteins are functional. The summary (C44) accurately reflects the data presented in prior claims.

results.result: Restoration of LAT centrality to physiological levels enhances IL-2 mRNA production under attenuated conditions. Expression of targeting domains alone had minor effects on IL-2 mRNA. LAT V3, which forces exaggerated central clustering, did not affect IL-2 mRNA. However, LAT Vav and LAT PLCδPH, which restore LAT centrality to levels similar to full stimulus, yielded consistent and largely significant (p<0.05) increases in IL-2 mRNA. For example, upon costimulation blockade, LAT Vav restored IL-2 mRNA to 41±9% (wild type) and 58±10% (Itk-deficient) compared to 18±6% and 18±3% with non-targeted LAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 establish a critical functional link between LAT localization dynamics and IL-2 production. The controls (C45-C46) demonstrate specificity, and the rescue experiments (C47-C50) show that reconstitution of physiological LAT localization patterns, but not excessive central accumulation, enhances IL-2 production. The statistical analysis and quantitative data support the conclusion that central LAT accumulation extent and dynamics are important for IL-2 secretion (C51).

results.result: Forced central LAT localization by LAT V3 has limited and condition-dependent effects on recruitment of other signaling intermediates. Under full stimulus, LAT V3 moderately diminished interface recruitment of Grb2, Lck, and Vav1, suggesting excessive central LAT localization upsets signaling balance. Upon costimulation blockade, localization of these intermediates was largely unaffected. In Itk-deficient cells, Grb2 and Lck centrality was moderately enhanced at later time points. Only under the strongest attenuation (Itk deficiency plus costimulation blockade) was Grb2 substantially recruited to levels not seen under other conditions. Vav1 centrality was not altered under any condition.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C60 systematically characterize the effects of forced LAT localization on other signaling intermediates across multiple conditions. The imaging data demonstrate that LAT V3 cannot broadly recruit other proteins to the cSMAC, with effects being limited to proteins with some intrinsic central localization preference (Grb2, Lck) and only under specific conditions. The negative result for Vav1 (C59) provides an important specificity control. The inference that forced LAT localization can only modestly recruit certain intermediates (C60) is well-supported.

results.result: SLP-76 shows transient central accumulation that is enhanced by fusion with PKCθ V3 or Vav1 SH3SH2SH3 domains under attenuated conditions. Under full stimulus, 45±7% of cell couples displayed central SLP-76 accumulation at tight coupling, dropping to <10% after 80s. This peak was significantly diminished (p≤0.01) upon costimulation blockade, Itk deficiency, and their combination to <27%, <15%, and <11%, respectively. SLP-76 fusion constructs did not significantly affect centrality under full stimulus but moderately and significantly (p<0.05) enhanced central accumulation upon costimulation blockade, with enhancement limited to the first minute of coupling when non-targeted SLP-76 naturally accumulates centrally.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 characterize SLP-76 localization and the effects of fusion proteins with appropriate statistical analysis. The transient nature of SLP-76 central accumulation (C61-C62) contrasts with LAT's more sustained accumulation. The effects of attenuation (C63) and fusion proteins (C64-C66) are well-documented. Importantly, the temporal restriction of fusion protein effects to the natural window of SLP-76 central accumulation (C66) suggests that fusion domains can enhance but not fundamentally alter intrinsic localization preferences.

results.result: Enhancement of SLP-76 centrality modestly increases IL-2 mRNA production under costimulation blockade. Expression of SLP-76 V3 and SLP-76 Vav resulted in modest increases in IL-2 mRNA under costimulation blocked conditions. Upon costimulation blockade, non-targeted SLP-76 expression reduced IL-2 mRNA to 45±9% (wild type) and 21±1% (Itk-deficient) of full stimulus. SLP-76 V3 restored IL-2 mRNA to 87±20% and 74±24%, and SLP-76 Vav to 73±8% and 75±30%, though without reaching statistical significance in 2-way ANOVA. Enhancement of centrality and IL-2 secretion remained closely linked across conditions and constructs.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C71 show trends toward IL-2 mRNA restoration with SLP-76 fusion proteins, but the lack of statistical significance in the stringent 2-way ANOVA (C69-C70) weakens the conclusion. The correlation between centrality and IL-2 production (C71) is noted, but without statistical significance for the IL-2 measurements, the functional importance of SLP-76 centrality enhancement remains uncertain. Additional experiments or less stringent statistical tests might clarify this result.

results.result: Grb2 fusion proteins do not enhance central accumulation or IL-2 production, providing a negative control. Under full stimulus, Grb2 is efficiently recruited to the interface (80±5% of cell couples) but central accumulation doesn't exceed 20% under any condition. Interface accumulation was significantly diminished (p≤0.02) upon costimulation blockade, Itk deficiency, and both. Fusion with PKCθ V3 or Vav1 SH3SH2SH3 did not enhance centrality under any condition. Grb2 V3 did not substantially alter localization, while Grb2 Vav enhanced overall interface recruitment (mostly peripheral pattern) but not centrality. Neither fusion protein altered IL-2 mRNA production despite enhanced interface accumulation by Grb2 Vav.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C81 provide a critical negative control demonstrating that proteins with minor intrinsic central preference cannot be forced to the cSMAC (C79) and that enhanced interface accumulation without central localization does not affect IL-2 production (C80-C81). The imaging and functional data are consistent and well-controlled. This specificity control strengthens the conclusions about the functional importance of central accumulation for LAT and SLP-76.

results.result: The cSMAC consists of multiple supramolecular complexes with dynamically changing composition that enhances early T cell activation and may attenuate later signaling. The cSMAC is driven by extensive membrane undulations and contains compositionally rich complexes during the first two minutes of cell coupling that enhance T cell activation by facilitating efficient signaling interactions. Thereafter, compositionally poorer complexes may sequester signaling intermediates.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C84 provide a summary model integrating structural and functional data. The structural characterization (C82) is well-supported by STED and electron microscopy data. The time-dependent functional model (C83-C84) is supported by the correlation between early central accumulation and IL-2 production, and the observation that excessive sustained central accumulation (LAT V3) does not enhance IL-2 production. However, the sequestration hypothesis for later time points (C84) is speculative and not directly tested.

results.result: The cSMAC has properties of supramolecular protein complexes based on prior work. The cSMAC contains various multivalent signaling intermediates including LAT, components exchange with the cell moderately and slowly, and components can be assembled into supramolecular structures in vitro.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C88 summarize prior work characterizing cSMAC properties. The claims are supported by appropriate citations to previous studies. This provides important context for the current work but does not constitute new findings from this manuscript.

results.result: Prior work has shown that central accumulation of signaling intermediates is reduced under various conditions of attenuated T cell activation. Accumulation at the T cell:APC interface center is substantially reduced by CD28 blockade, in regulatory T cells, during thymic selection, and in the absence of Itk.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C92 summarize prior work establishing that central protein accumulation is associated with T cell activation strength. The claims are supported by appropriate citations. This provides important context and rationale for the current study but does not constitute new findings.

results.result: Supramolecular protein complexes play critical roles in diverse biological processes based on prior work. These include viral sensing, inflammation, embryonic development, protein folding in cancer, nuclear ubiquitinoylation, and chromatin compaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C98 cite prior work on supramolecular complexes in various biological contexts. The claims provide general background on the importance of supramolecular complexes but do not constitute findings from this manuscript.

results.result: Prior work has shown that receptor clusters at the nanoscale are associated with active signaling intermediates and may mediate efficient T cell signaling. Receptors form clusters of dozens of molecules that can coalesce into microclusters and are commonly associated with active forms of signaling intermediates.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 summarize prior work on nanoscale receptor clustering. The association with active signaling intermediates (C99) is supported by citations, while the inference about mediating efficient signaling (C100) is reasonable but not directly demonstrated in the cited work. This provides context for the current study's focus on micrometer-scale organization.

results.result: The cSMAC and pSMAC were first described in prior work as micrometer-scale assemblies at the center and periphery of T cells activated by APCs, containing TCR/PKCθ and LFA-1/talin, respectively.
results.evaluation: Claim C101 cites the original descriptions of the cSMAC and pSMAC. This provides important historical context for the current work but does not constitute a new finding.
